entries.title: One dominant visual device

inputs.purpose: The intended feeling and attention target.
The change that the visual strategy must carry.

entries.outputIntent: Choose one visual device that carries the scene and keep other devices supportive.
guidance: Translate the intended audience effect into one dominant choice in composition, camera, light, color, or rhythm.
Let that device change with the scene turn; avoid simultaneous unrelated changes that compete for attention.
verifyCriteria: The dominant device is named and motivated by the scene.
Supporting choices do not compete with it.
incompatibilities: Multiple unrelated dominant devices in the same beat.

entries.title: Motivated camera grammar

inputs.purpose: What changes in the subject or audience attention.

entries.outputIntent: Select camera position, distance, and movement that have a visible reason.
guidance: Use distance to control intimacy and angle to control the subject's relationship to the world.
Move only when subject movement, attention, discovery, or emotional escalation motivates the move.
verifyCriteria: The camera plan states why the camera is where it is.
Any move has one readable motivation and endpoint.
incompatibilities: Decorative movement with no beat-level motivation.

entries.title: Question-and-response editing

inputs.purpose: Approved observable beats in intended order.

entries.outputIntent: Build a cut sequence in which each edit answers or sharpens the prior shot.
guidance: Cut on action for continuity, on a look for discovery, and to a reaction when consequence carries the scene.
Remove a shot that neither answers an active question nor creates the next one.
verifyCriteria: Every cut has a narrative, emotional, rhythmic, or attention function.
Reaction coverage is preserved where it carries the consequence.
incompatibilities: Coverage retained only because it was generated.

entries.title: Motivated light with emotional purpose

inputs.purpose: Light sources that exist in the scene world.
The emotional and attention purpose of the light.

entries.outputIntent: Define a coherent key, fill relationship, separation, and continuity state.
guidance: Start from an in-world source and exaggerate it only in service of attention or emotion.
Record direction, quality, temperature, and continuity so adjacent material remains matchable.
verifyCriteria: The key source is legible in the scene world.
Light direction and state remain coherent across coverage.
incompatibilities: Unexplained fill or direction changes between matching shots.

entries.title: Color as story arc

inputs.purpose: Approved sections or sequences and their emotional changes.

entries.outputIntent: Create a restrained palette progression whose changes correspond to story changes.
guidance: Define temperature and saturation per block rather than treating color as isolated decoration.
Establish recurring accent meaning before transferring or reversing it.
verifyCriteria: Every material palette shift has a story reason.
A recurring accent remains semantically consistent until deliberately changed.

entries.title: Pacing through duration and processing

inputs.purpose: Relative emotional and informational weight of each beat.

entries.outputIntent: Allocate screen time so anticipation, action, and visible processing remain legible.
guidance: Shorten duration as pressure rises and hold when the audience must absorb a peak or consequence.
Treat silence and stillness as authored beats, not empty time.
verifyCriteria: The longest holds land on material attention or emotional work.
Heavy events receive visible processing before new information arrives.
incompatibilities: Uniform pacing that ignores beat weight.

provenance.adaptation: Rewritten as compact, format-neutral recipes with explicit inputs, output intent, and verification.
